cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pulled a chair out like you. Seats saved. I wasn't just late to the reunion; can I tell you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I moved that chair so people could get past. At the reunion I did save you one. Was it traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the way clear, then. I waited outside for half an hour. Will you hear why?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd enjoy yourself more without me. Will you sit beside me now?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies chair movement as saving seats; A3 directs clear passage after correction while revealing wait; A5 admits fear of unwanted presence after B4 hurt.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 traffic guess leads A3 true delay without misleading yes; B4 felt-rejected account leads A5 deeper insecurity.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers remembered saved seat and B4 honestly names hurt.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 mistaken rejection to test current support with a more vulnerable explanation.

specificity.evidence: A1 current chairs and B2 past reunion are distinguished.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 clean imperative removes false affirmation; A5 seat request is immediate.
